This query separates committed-high persistence from rolled-back high puts.", "proposed_change": "Model sqlite_sequence as a durable counter updated only by committed inserts (and possibly by rolled-back inserts in this SQLite build), not by transient max(rows); rollback must restore prior rows and sequence state."}}
policy.scope: Distinguish durable AUTOINCREMENT sequence advancement from transient row-set maxima across commit, delete, and rollback.
policy.change: Probe committed high ID 9, delete it, then rollback an uncommitted put 2; parent predicts 10 from max seen, while a durable sqlite_sequence model predicts 10 only if sequence persists, making the rollback branch discriminating.

note.obligation: Return the AUTOINCREMENT id allocated by a final implicit insert after mixed transactional put/delete actions.
note.suspected_boundary: Parent tracks only max inserted id and ignores rollback of committed state plus later uncommitted puts; sqlite_sequence should persist at 9 after delete and rollback.
note.evidence: Known receipts: rollback of put 9 gives 1, while rollback after committed put 3 then put 11 gives 4; parent answers 10 and 12 respectively. This query separates committed-high persistence from rolled-back high puts.
note.proposed_change: Model sqlite_sequence as a durable counter updated only by committed inserts (and possibly by rolled-back inserts in this SQLite build), not by transient max(rows); rollback must restore prior rows and sequence state.
